Use this instead of inventing block markup yourself: Kadence bakes every uniqueID into the block's class names and encodes the JSON in the block comment in its own way, and hand-written markup is guaranteed to deviate from that. post_id is required because the uniqueIDs must be unique within the post the section goes into; two blocks with the same ID share their CSS and change together. The built markup is parsed and re-serialized before it is returned, and if it doesn't come out identical, you get an error instead of markup. If the design fits none of the recipes — a hero with a label above the heading, a section with colored bars, columns that each have their own background — use recipe custom and pass the tree via tree; build what belongs together in one go. ONE: switching block type, for example kadence/query-filter to kadence/query-filter-buttons. Removing and reinserting can do that too, but produces a new uniqueID, and references hang off it that nobody updates — a Query Loop's facets are stored in post meta and point to the filter block by uniqueID. If that ID changes, the filter stops working and there is no error message anywhere. TWO: changing an attribute that markup derives from, such as direction on a column or colorClass on a heading. set-attributes only touches the block comment, so a derived class stays at the old value; here the markup is rebuilt from the block profile, so those classes come along. Only works on block types whose markup is known; describe-block doesn't list them, list-recipes does. The children stay by default and move along. If the block type stays the same, the existing attributes are merged with what you provide; if you switch type, they do NOT carry over, because an attribute of the old block doesn't necessarily exist on the new one — so specify explicitly what the new block should get. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal showing the old and new first line side by side, then again with that token to write. Start here: describe-block only makes sense once you know which block exists. Blocks that may only appear inside another block carry that in "parent" or "ancestor", and the two are not the same: parent says which block it may sit DIRECTLY inside, ancestor that it must sit somewhere BELOW that block. The query blocks may sit directly in a Section, but only if that Section itself sits below a kadence/query — that is why they only appear in the editor once you are inside the Query Loop.

Geeft alles wat je van een posttype moet: Returns everything you need to know about a post type to build a Query Loop and a Query Card on it: how many published posts there are, which taxonomies are attached and how many terms they have, which meta fields a real post of this type carries, and the fixed fields Kadence itself offers in dynamic blocks. Call this BEFORE you set up a card. A Query Card displays fields with kadence/dynamichtml, which needs the meta key; a wrong key produces an empty block without any error message. Note the difference with get-post-meta: that one deliberately returns only Kadence keys, which is right for block work but useless as soon as you build a Loop over another post type — the fields you need then come from an entirely different plugin. The values here are truncated: this is meant to show WHICH field you need, not to read out content. With source acf the field belongs to Advanced Custom Fields; in both cases you reference it with field post|post_custom_field, para kb_custom_input, and custom equal to the key.
Geeft de attributen van één blok: type,: Returns the attributes of one block: type, default value, allowed values, and the group the attribute belongs to. Large blocks are paginated — kadence/rowlayout has well over 170. CAUTION when searching: "search" matches on the attribute NAME, and Kadence often stores responsive values in an array [desktop, tablet, mobile] under one name. The attribute that sets the mobile direction of a Section is called "direction", not "mobileDirection" — so searching for "mobile" won't find it. If you want to be sure what a block can do, filter on "group" or fetch everything with per_page 100. A default value that is itself a large structure is summarized.
Geeft de opgeslagen post_content terug,: Returns the saved post_content, or that of a single block. Needed because the other tools only show parsed ATTRIBUTES, and whether an attribute is safe to change depends on what is in the MARKUP. A block saved as self-closing (ending in /-->) has no markup of its own and is free to change; a block with a wrapper usually bakes its uniqueID into a class name and is not. Use this before you propose a write, and use max_chars to avoid fetching an entire styled page.
Geeft de post meta van een post terug, b: Returns the post meta of a post, limited to keys that belong to Kadence (_kad_, _kt_, kadence_). This is needed because a large part of the Kadence configuration is NOT in block attributes. The clearest example is kadence/query: that block has only six attributes and none of them is about the query — post type, sort order, meta_key and filters are in _kad_query_query on the kadence_query post. Without this tool you can see that a Query Loop is there but not how it is configured. Meta from other plugins is deliberately not returned; the number of omitted keys is in withheld.
Geeft de sjablonen die generate-section: Returns the recipes generate-section knows, listing for each recipe the blocks it uses and the slots you can fill. Request this before having a section built, so you pass the right slug and the right fields. The recipes deliberately supply only the STRUCTURE: the right blocks, nested correctly, with working uniqueIDs, and nothing else. No colors, margins, or font sizes are filled in — those come from the global styles, and a made-up value is noise someone has to track down later. Do the styling afterward with set-attributes.
Geeft een AI-assistent toegang tot Kaden: Gives an AI assistant access to Kadence via MCP: twenty-three read tools and twenty-five write tools. Everything is off by default; you turn on, per tool, what you want to offer. Writing additionally requires the capability kadence_mcp_write, which is granted to no one on installation.
Geeft het globale kleurenpalet, de basis: Returns the global color palette, the base typography, and the site-wide default settings per block. The latter are INSERTION defaults: what the editor fills in for a new block, and what ends up in the markup on save. They change nothing about existing blocks — a missing attribute there still means the default value from describe-block. What they are for is knowing what form something should take on this site when you propose something new. If a source is missing, that is stated as such — no values are made up. Also useful for knowing which color a block means when it refers to "palette3". WARNING about typography: the theme fills in an unset key with its default value, so a value does not mean it has been set — typography_sources says per key whether it is saved or default. fonts lists the font faces the site itself provides (Kadence Custom Fonts) and warns if a family or weight from the typography has none; the browser then silently falls back or synthesizes the weight. environment also gives the child theme version and whether a page cache is running (clear it first before you treat a difference after a release as a bug).

Kopieert een bestaand blok, met alles er: Copies an existing block, with everything below it, to another post and gives each copy a new uniqueID prefixed with the target post. This is the safest way to build something: the markup comes from the editor and is therefore valid, and nothing is made up. Use this for recreate-this-layout. The uniqueID appears in two places — in the attribute and woven into classes such as kadence-column..., kb-btns..., and data-kb-block — and both are replaced together, so no mismatch can occur. By default this is a DRY RUN: it shows the markup it would insert, the map from old to new uniqueID, and a token. To write, pass dry_run false plus that same token AND that same id_map — the map must be included, otherwise fresh IDs would be generated and you would write something other than what you saw. Before writing, it checks that the map covers exactly the blocks to be copied, contains no duplicate values, and does not collide with IDs already in the target post. Otherwise the same safeguards apply as for set-attributes. After writing, it reads back and checks that every copied block is actually there.

Leest de blokstructuur van een post zond: Reads the block structure of a post without changing it. Works on regular pages and posts as well as the Kadence post types. Returns, for each block, the name, the nesting depth, the number of child blocks, and a limited set of attributes — by default uniqueID, id, className, align, and metadata. metadata contains the name from List View and blockVisibility; if the latter is false, the block is hidden with WordPress's native hide option, and nothing else shows that. Large or nested attribute values are summarized; to see one untruncated, name it in full_attributes. Request extra attributes selectively — a full dump of a styled page runs to thousands of lines. You only get the visible text with include_text: blocks such as kadence/listitem and kadence/advancedheading store their text in the markup, not in an attribute. A block without a uniqueID (core blocks, the Gravity Forms form block) gets a path field, for example "pad:3.0.1": that is its position in the tree, and validate-write, set-attributes, style-blocks, get-raw-markup, and from_unique_id accept it in place of a uniqueID. A path shifts when blocks are added or removed before it; the token catches that because it is tied to the modified date.
Leest een Kadence-object uit als één pak: Reads out a Kadence object as a single package: the blocks in post_content and the display settings in _kad meta (shadows, colors, placement, widths) — the part that get-raw-markup and prepare-import don't include. Also lists the posts and media it references, with type, title, slug, or file name, so you can look up their counterpart on the other site. Then pass the package to import-entity on the other site. Writes nothing.
Leest een kadence_query volledig uit en: Reads a kadence_query in full and puts the three layers side by side. ONE: what the query fetches, from the post meta _kad_query_query — post type, number per page, sort order. TWO: which filter blocks are in the layout. THREE: the facets in _kad_query_facets, the derived description the front end reads to know which taxonomy a filter shows. That third layer is the pitfall of this block: it is NOT in the markup and the editor recalculates it from the blocks on every change. If it gets out of sync, the page has a filter that does nothing, without any error message. This ability therefore recalculates the facets the same way the editor does and reports the difference. It also does a dry run: the query is actually executed so you can see how many posts it returns — the meta has no schema, so saved does not mean valid there, and a post type that does not exist simply produces an empty page.
Empty CSS would erase everything that is there. If you really want that, pass a space; if you want to add something, turn on append.
Let op: deze post komt niet terug uit ee: Note: this post is not returned by a normal query for this account — a plugin such as Members is probably hiding it. So find-post does not find it, while this tool does read it.
Let op: er zijn onopgeloste verwijzingen: Note: there are unresolved references, and they have been accepted with accept_warnings.
Letterlijke vervangingen, in volgorde to: Literal replacements, applied in order to all text in attributes and markup. Example: [{"from":"https://oud.example","to":"https://nieuw.example"},{"from":"kb-custom-112","to":"kb-custom-87"}]. Don't replace bare numbers — "112" also appears in dimensions.
Lezen uit Kadence Blocks, Kadence Blocks: Read from Kadence Blocks, Kadence Blocks Pro, Kadence Pro, and the Kadence theme.
Loopt alle verwijzingen in een post na e: Goes through all references in a post and reports for each one whether it is valid, dangling, or cannot be verified. Needed because Kadence logs nothing and shows no error message: a broken dynamic reference makes the block silently disappear, and an invalid post type in a Query Loop falls back to blog posts. Checks five places, because the same setting is often stored twice: the regular attributes field, tax, metaField and customMeta; the kadenceDynamic object per slot; the same link again as a kb-dynamic-shortcode in the target attribute; inline spans with data-field in the markup; and the post meta _kad_query_query and _kad_query_facets. References to standalone Kadence objects (query, card, navigation, header) are also checked for existence, post type, and publication status.
Loopt de blokattributen van alle posts,: Goes through the block attributes of all posts, the _kad meta of the Kadence objects, and the theme typography, and groups by color value where it is used (post:ID uniqueID attribute, or meta:ID key). For each value, the `soort` (kind): palette (palette3), palette variable (var(--global-palette3)), variable (var(--custom-token)), hex, or rgb. A hex that equals a palette color gets same_as: it looks right but does not change along with the palette. With only_off_palette, only hex, rgb and the rest; with value, only that one value. Colors in the theme's CSS files are not shown here. Writes nothing; convert afterward with style-blocks or set-entity-meta.
Loopt een post na en meldt elk blok waar: Walks through a post and reports every block whose classes in the markup no longer match its attributes. Do this after every series of write actions, and especially after changing an attribute that markup derives from. Why this is needed: Kadence derives classes from attributes, but set-attributes and style-blocks only touch the block comment. So after such a change there is a class that no longer matches the attribute. On the FRONT END this goes unnoticed, because there the attribute drives the display and the old class does nothing. In the EDITOR it doesn't: the editor compares the saved markup with what the block itself would write, and calls the difference unexpected or invalid content. If the user then clicks block recovery, Kadence renumbers all uniqueIDs and outside references come loose — for a Query Loop, that breaks the link with the facets. This ability fixes nothing; it returns the uniqueIDs you can rebuild with replace-block. Only block types whose profile is known are checked, and only on classes; checked says how many blocks were actually checked.
Maakt een nieuw Kadence-object aan, zoda: Creates a new Kadence object, so you can then put blocks in it (prepare-import or generate-section, then insert-blocks) and write settings to it (set-entity-meta). Needed when migrating to another environment: the navigations, headers, and elements don't exist there yet, and blocks that reference them need their new ID (post_map in prepare-import). A navigation, header, or element is created EMPTY, but with ALL the settings Kadence registers for that post type, at their default value — otherwise set-entity-meta refuses them later, because a key that isn't there could be a typo or an unknown setting. Use meta to set non-default settings right away (only keys Kadence registers for this post type). A vector is created from svg, via Kadence's own route (kb-vector/v1/vectors) and therefore through Kadence's sanitizer; it is always published. Status defaults to draft: a published element with a hook such as replace_footer immediately replaces the footer of the entire site, even while it is still empty. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal, then with the token to create.
Maakt een nieuwe Query Card door een bes: Creates a new Query Card by copying an existing one. A Query Card is the layout of ONE result in a Query Loop and is a separate post of type kadence_query_card; the Loop refers to it with an id in the kadence/query-card block. If you want a Loop over a different post type, you almost always need a separate card too, because the fields differ. Copy rather than build from scratch: a card is full of dynamic blocks — kadence/dynamichtml for a field, kadence/dynamiclist for taxonomy terms, a button with a kb-dynamic-shortcode as its link — and adjusting those relationships is easier than inventing them. Pass for_post_type so the card shows a preview of the right kind of post in the editor; if that is wrong, every dynamic field looks empty even though nothing is wrong. Adjust it afterward with set-attributes and replace-block, and describe-post-type shows which fields are available to display. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal, then with the token.
Maakt een nieuwe Query Loop door een bes: Creates a new Query Loop by copying an existing one, or with a preset (no-filters or simple) following the templates of Kadence's selection screen, with an existing card. Copy rather than build from scratch, for the same reason as with duplicate-blocks: the layout comes from the editor and is therefore valid, and a Query Loop is tied to a query card that is itself a separate post — that reference simply stays in place in a copy. What happens: the blocks are carried over with FRESH uniqueIDs prefixed with the new post, all _kad_query settings are copied along, and then the facets are recalculated. That last step is not optional — the facets point to the filter blocks by uniqueID, and those have all just changed; if you left them as they were, every filter in the new query would point to a block that does not exist. With settings you can immediately set what the new query fetches. Placing it on a page is something you do yourself afterward: use generate-section to build a custom tree with a single kadence/query block and the id of the new query, and insert that with insert-blocks. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal, then with the token to actually create it.
Creates a new page with block content. As a DRAFT by default: what an agent writes is a first draft, and a page that goes live immediately is visible to everyone with a single call. Publishing is a separate, deliberate step — set status to publish only if that is explicitly intended, and even then it refuses without the capability publish_pages. With parent_id the page goes under an existing page, which determines the URL: under a page with the slug evenementen it becomes /evenementen/<slug>/. The markup is checked the same way as with insert-blocks: first parse, then re-serialize, and compare. If something different comes out, WordPress would rewrite the markup on save and what you see would not match what is stored; in that case nothing is created. Don't build that markup by hand but with generate-section, because Kadence bakes every uniqueID into the class names. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal, then with the token.
Maakt één post aan van een posttype dat: Creates one post of a post type that exists on this site and is in the REST API: post or a custom post type. Not for pages (create-page), attachments, or Kadence's own post types (create-entity, create-query, create-query-card). One ability for all post types, because what differs per type is defined in WordPress itself and is read out and validated here on each call: excerpt, menu_order, and featured_image only if the post type supports them; terms only for taxonomies attached to this post type, with terms that exist (by slug or ID); acf only for fields from an ACF field group that applies to this post type, by field name, and a relationship field only with IDs of existing posts of an allowed type. Anything that doesn't check out is refused instead of being saved silently. content is optional block markup and goes through the same parse-and-serialize check as create-page. A draft by default. When migrating to another environment: first create the posts that others reference, and use their new IDs in post_map of prepare-import. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal, then with the token to create.

Neemt blokmarkup aan die NIET door gener: Accepts block markup that was NOT built by generate-section — serialized in the editor, read out with get-raw-markup on another site, or from a pattern — and prepares it to be placed in this post with insert-blocks. Writes nothing itself. What happens, in order: (1) blocks only, no loose HTML, and every block type must exist on this site; (2) the markup must survive a parse-and-serialize round trip; (3) every uniqueID gets a new value with the post prefix of THIS post, in the attribute and in the classes, and the map is in id_map; (4) the classes in the markup must match the attributes, for every block type whose profile is known — the same check as verify-markup; (5) every attribute goes through the schema check and the value lists of validate-write; (6) counters such as slideCount and tabCount must equal the number of child blocks; (7) everything that points outward is reported: links to another domain, images and media IDs that don't exist here, custom SVG icons (kb-custom-N), terms, references to other posts (navigations, headers, queries, query cards, vectors, forms, menu items pointing to a post) that don't exist here or are a different type, palette colors with their value on THIS site, and the custom CSS classes the markup uses. Conversion only happens explicitly: replace for literal text (a different domain, a different icon ID), media_map, term_map, and post_map for IDs; nothing is guessed. The verdict `veilig` (safe) returns a token for insert-blocks. With `blokkeer` (block) there is no token. With `riskant` (risky) — a reference that doesn't exist on this site — only with accept_warnings true, and that is a decision for a human. What this check CANNOT do: prove that the editor will consider the block valid, because that check exists only in the block's JavaScript. So open the post in the editor once after inserting.

Schrijft attributen naar meerdere blokke: Writes attributes to multiple blocks at once. Use this as soon as you style more than one block — styling a section quickly touches the row, the column, the text blocks, and the buttons, and doing that with set-attributes takes two calls per block plus a token that expires at every intermediate step because the post has changed in the meantime. Works in two steps: first call it without a token and each block is checked individually with exactly the same checks as validate-write, after which you get the verdict for each block; then call it again with the token and everything is written in a single save, so one revision. All or nothing: if any block is `blokkeer` (block) or `riskant` (risky), no token is issued and nothing is written — applying it halfway leaves the page in a state nobody intended. A block that appears twice in the list is rejected. Attributes equal to the default value are dropped — that is what the editor does too — and are reported in defaults, not in mismatch. Requires the kadence_mcp_write capability and edit permission on the post.
Schrijft attributen naar één bestaand bl: Writes attributes to one existing block. If you are styling more than one block at once, use style-blocks: it saves calls and produces one revision instead of a series, and any intermediate token here would expire anyway as soon as the previous step changed the post. Requires the kadence_mcp_write capability, edit permission on the post according to WordPress, and a valid token from validate-write — without that token it refuses, and the token is bound to this post, this block, these exact attributes, and the post's modified date. If you change anything in your proposal, you must validate again. So the order is always: validate-write, preview-write, and only then this. Attributes equal to the default value are omitted and the rest are placed in block schema order, exactly as the editor would do it. After saving, the post is read back and compared with what was intended; if it differs, that is reported in mismatch. A revision is created, so you can roll back.
Schrijft naar Weergave > Customizer > Ex: Writes to Appearance > Customizer > Additional CSS. That is the only place in WordPress itself where CSS is served on EVERY page. It exists because the Custom CSS field on a Kadence header or element DOES exist but is not served on the front end; that was measured on 14-09-2026 and resulted in CSS that ended up nowhere. Use this for rules that apply across the whole site, such as positioning a dropdown menu. If the rule belongs to the design of the theme itself, put it in the child theme's stylesheet instead — that is under version control and this field is not. Replaces the entire content by default; turn on append to add it below. WARNING: the previous content is in the before field and is the only way to revert. Two steps: first without a token, then with it.
Somt op wat Kadence als eigen posttype b: Lists what Kadence stores as its own post types: kadence_header, kadence_element, kadence_navigation, kadence_form, kadence_lottie, and whatever else is registered. Use this to get a post_id that you can then open with inspect-post. WARNING: this lists only KADENCE post types, not a regular page or post — you need to get the post_id of a regular page elsewhere. The list is discovered by prefix plus a short exception list, so a new Kadence post type appears automatically.

Toegang tot Kadence Blocks, Kadence Bloc: Access to Kadence Blocks, Kadence Blocks Pro, Kadence Pro, and the Kadence theme. Forty-nine abilities: twenty-three read, twenty-six write. SO WRITING IS NOT THE EXCEPTION — for every tool you call, read in its description whether it writes. Every write ability requires the capability kadence_mcp_write (which is granted to no one after installation), edit permission on the post according to WordPress itself, and a token from a preceding check step (only style-blocks and set-text accept expect_modified instead, the post_modified_gmt you already know: that is one call instead of two — use it if you have just read the post); afterwards the result is read back and compared. What they touch differs: most write post_content, but set-entity-meta and set-card-layout write post meta (no revisions), and set-global-typography and set-site-css affect the whole site. If you are styling more than one block at a time, use style-blocks: set-attributes does one block per call, and each token expires as soon as the post changes. To build a new section, do not make up markup; ask for list-recipes and generate-section: Kadence bakes each uniqueID into the block's class names, and hand-written markup is guaranteed to be wrong. Markup that the editor wrote itself, or that comes from another site, goes through prepare-import: it checks it, converts the uniqueIDs, reports what differs per site, converts media, term, and post IDs using a supplied map, and returns a token for insert-blocks. A navigation, header, element, or vector that does not yet exist on the target site is created first with create-entity; a regular post (post, service, market) with terms and ACF fields with create-post, and an existing one is updated with update-post. Moving blocks within a post while preserving uniqueID is done with move-blocks.
Toetst een VOORGENOMEN attribuutwijzigin: Checks a PROPOSED attribute change on one block, without changing anything. Always call this before you propose a change to the user. Checks for each attribute: does it exist on this block, does the value fit the declared type and allowed values, is the attribute parsed from the markup (then writing is a silent no-op), and does the current value appear literally in the saved markup (then the markup needs to change too, and changing only the attribute is a silent break). In addition, it knows three attributes with their own failure path: uniqueID, kbVersion, and columns. For uniqueID it also checks for collisions — Kadence itself only does that in the editor and only within the post that is open. With the verdict `veilig` (safe), a token is returned that is bound to this post, this block, these exact attributes, and the current modified date; a later write action requires that token, so the check cannot be skipped and you cannot write anything other than what was checked.

Vergelijkt twee blokken op hun uniqueID: Compares two blocks by their uniqueID and returns only the differences, sorted by group. Always use this when the question is why two things look different — for example two mega menus or two sections. Fetching a selection of attributes yourself and comparing them is unreliable: you miss whatever you didn't request. The two blocks may be in the same post or in different ones; leave out post_id_b if it is the same post. An attribute that is set on only one of the two appears with null on the other side — that means "not set", so the block's default value applies there.
Verplaatst blokken (met alles eronder) n: Moves blocks (with everything below them) to a new location in the same post: before or after another block, or as the first or last child inside a container. The uniqueIDs stay put, so the per-block CSS and references to them (facets, anchors) keep working; removing and reinserting would produce new IDs. Multiple blocks land in the new location in the order given. Refuses if the target lies inside one of the blocks being moved, if a Section (kadence/column) would move out of or into a Row Layout (the row's column count would no longer be correct), and if a block's parent rule doesn't allow it under the new parent. Before writing, it checks that no block disappears. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal, then with the token. A revision is created.
Verplaatst en teruggelezen: de blokken s: Moved and read back: the blocks are in the new location, and all uniqueIDs are still there. A revision has been created.
Vervangt de tekst van één blok. Nodig om: Replaces the text of one block. Needed because the text of a heading or paragraph is not in the attributes but in the innerHTML: set-attributes rightly refuses that, because the classes and data attributes are also built from it. This ability touches only the part inside the outermost tag and leaves that tag exactly as is, so Gutenberg's block validation still passes. Works in two steps, not three: first call it without a token and you get back the old text, the new text, and a token without anything being saved; then call it again with that token and it writes. A separate validate step would add nothing here, because there is no schema to check a text against. Refuses a block with child blocks, an innerHTML that is not exactly one wrapping element, and an empty text. For a kadence/listitem, only the text in .kt-svg-icon-list-text is replaced; the link and icon stay in place. HTML in the text is reduced by wp_kses to formatting tags such as strong, em, a, br, span, and mark; whatever is removed is listed in notes. Requires the kadence_mcp_write capability. A revision is created.
Verwijdert een of meer blokken uit een p: Removes one or more blocks from a post, at any depth — even a single button from a button row. Note that a container takes everything below it with it: removing a row removes its columns and their content. That's why it works in two steps: call it first without a token and you'll see exactly which blocks would disappear and what text they contain, without anything happening; then call it again with that token to actually do it. If any of the given uniqueIDs is not in the post, nothing is removed — a request that is half right is not half carried out. Requires the capability kadence_mcp_write and edit permission on the post. A revision is created, so you can roll back.

Voegt blokmarkup toe aan een bestaande p: Adds block markup to an existing post, at a location you choose. Requires the capability kadence_mcp_write, edit permission on the post, and the token from generate-section or prepare-import — that token is bound to this post, this exact markup, and the post's modified date, so markup you have changed yourself won't get in. Before saving, it checks that every uniqueID already in the post is still there afterward and that no duplicate uniqueIDs arise; if that doesn't hold, nothing is written. After saving, the post is read back. A revision is created, so you can roll back.

Voor de twee Kadence-objecten waarvan de: For the two Kadence objects whose content isn't blocks: a kadence_vector (bare SVG) and a kadence_custom_svg (an icon as JSON, for example kb-custom-112). Pass replace as a list of {from, to, count}: count is the number of times from must currently appear, and if that doesn't match, nothing happens — that way you don't accidentally replace something else. For a vector, it calculates in advance whether kses (without unfiltered_html) would strip elements; for a custom SVG, the JSON must remain valid. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal (with the current content in before), then with the token. The result is read back.
Voor het vergelijken van twee sites (lok: For comparing two sites (local and staging) on what is not in the blocks and what a pixel comparison only reveals later: palette, typography (with saved or default), fonts, terms with their description, whether taxonomies are publicly queryable, Kadence objects (per title a hash of content and meta, without IDs and domain), active plugins with version, and the reading settings. Run it on both sites and compare the hashes; where one differs, request again with detail: true and compare that part. Writes nothing.

Werkt de post meta _kad_query_facets bij: Updates the post meta _kad_query_facets so it matches the filter blocks in the layout again. Do this after EVERY change to the blocks of a kadence_query that involves a filter block: adding, removing, changing its type, or choosing a different taxonomy. The editor does this automatically; if you write the blocks through this MCP, it does not happen automatically and a filter that does nothing is left behind. The calculation is the same as the editor's, including the hash function, and the resulting facets are fully derived — there is nothing to choose here. Kadence picks up the change itself: as soon as this meta changes, the indexer updates the index, and that happens in the background, so a filter may be empty for a moment. Two steps: first without a token to see what would change, then with the token to write.
Wijst elke dynamische koppeling, taxonom: Does every dynamic link, taxonomy filter, and object reference still point to something that exists?
Wijzigt de INSTELLINGEN van een Kadence-: Changes the SETTINGS of a Kadence entity: a navigation, an element, a header, a query, or a query card. These are not in the block markup but in post meta with the prefix _kad_, and no block ability can reach them. That is the difference between "what is in the menu" (blocks, so set-attributes) and "how the menu looks" (meta, so here): the link color of a navigation, the width of a dropdown, and for an element the placement — which hook, on which pages it shows and on which it does not. Read get-post-meta first: a key that is not listed there is rejected, because Kadence writes out its entire set on save, so a missing key is either a typo or a setting this entity does not know. Such a key would be silently saved and then ignored, and that looks as if it worked. WARNING: post meta has no revisions. Reverting is only possible with the values from the before field of the response, so keep them. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal with old and new side by side, then again with that token to write. The result is read back. The same change on multiple entities (the link color of six navigations) can be done at once with items: [{post_id, meta}, …] — one proposal, one token.
Wijzigt de RASTERINSTELLINGEN van een Qu: Changes the GRID SETTINGS of a Query Card. These are not in the block markup but in post meta on the card itself, and no other ability can reach them: set-attributes and style-blocks only touch blocks. Without this ability, a copied card is therefore stuck with the number of columns of its source, and that is exactly where a Query Loop over another post type breaks down — the card works, but everything is stacked. Note the difference with the card content: how a single result looks is controlled with set-attributes and replace-block on the blocks INSIDE the card; how many results sit side by side is controlled here. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal with the old and new values side by side, then again with that token to write. The result is read back after writing.
Wijzigt de basistypografie van het Kaden: Changes the base typography of the Kadence theme: base_font, heading_font, and h1_font through h6_font. This is the only place where you can do something about headings that do NOT get their own size — theme text, form labels, headings in an accordion. Note the scope: a kadence/advancedheading with its own fontSize ignores these values completely, so this will not make existing hero headings smaller. Each key is an object with, among others, size and lineHeight, and each of those has a desktop, tablet, and mobile value. If mobile is missing, Kadence does NOT scale down and a phone gets the desktop size. What you provide is merged with what is there, not overwritten: specifying only size leaves family and weight alone. WARNING: these are theme mods and they have no revisions. Reverting is only possible with the values from the before field, so keep them. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal with old and new side by side, then again with that token.
Wijzigt de instellingen van een Query Lo: Changes the settings of a Query Loop: which post type it fetches, how many per page, in what order. This is not in the block markup but in the post meta _kad_query_query, and that meta has NO schema — a made-up key is saved just as readily as a valid one and then ignored, and a post type that does not exist produces an empty page with no error message. That is why two things happen here that are not needed elsewhere: unknown keys are rejected instead of passed through, and a DRY RUN is performed — the query is actually executed, before and after, so you can see how many posts it returns. If the new setting returns zero posts where the old one did return some, this is reported explicitly; it is not blocked, because zero may be intended. The keys you provide are merged with the existing settings, so you only need to send what changes. Two steps: first without a token, then with it.
Wijzigt de post_status van een pagina. B: Changes the post_status of a page. Exists because create-page could only set a status at CREATION: a page built as a draft could no longer be published afterward without the editor, which meant it couldn't be checked on the front end either. Publishing requires the capability publish_pages; not everyone has it, and that is on purpose. Be aware of what publishing means: the page is then visible to everyone and only gets its final slug from the title at that moment. If a page with that same slug already exists, WordPress appends a sequence number, so the URL differs from what you expected — the read-back url in the response is the truth, not your assumption. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal, then with the token.
WordPress keurt deze waarde af bij het r: WordPress rejects this value when rendering (%s) and then silently replaces it with the default value.
WordPress schrijft deze markup iets ande: WordPress writes this markup slightly differently from how it came in (usually only the encoding of the block comment). What comes back in markup is the form that will be saved.
Writing custom SVG content needs the unf: Writing custom SVG content needs the unfiltered_html capability. Upload or edit the icon in Kadence itself instead.
Zegt tegen WPML: post X is de vertaling: Tells WPML: post X is the translation of post Y. Exists because a translation created outside the translation editor (with the WordPress importer, with create-post, by hand) remains a standalone post: at most it gets a language, but it isn't linked to anything, and the language switcher then points nowhere. WPML Export and Import only links if the original itself carries the import fields, and those exist only in the export file, not in the database. This ability uses the official WPML hook wpml_set_element_language_details and touches nothing else: no content, no meta, no status. Both posts must exist and have the same post type, and that post type must be translatable in WPML. The language of the translation is the language WPML currently assigns to it; pass language if it is still in the original's language (for example right after an import). Refused: an original that already has another translation in that language (that one would end up unlinked), and a post that itself already has translations (those would move along). Multiple links can be made at once with items: one proposal, one token. Two steps: first without a token for a proposal with the current state of each link (before), then with the token to write. It is read back via WPML itself. There is no revision: rolling back means breaking the link in the editor (WPML's Language panel), with before as a reference.
Zet de header erin met insert-blocks: éé: Add the header with insert-blocks: one kadence/header block with its containers (prepare-import with the source markup). Assignment happens in the Customizer: Header, Header block.
Zet de inhoud erin met insert-blocks. De: Add the content with insert-blocks. The placement (hook, display rules) is in the meta; change it with set-entity-meta. Don't publish until the content is in place.
Zet de menu-items erin met insert-blocks: Add the menu items with insert-blocks: one kadence/navigation block containing the kadence/navigation-link blocks (prepare-import with the source markup, or generate-section). Then place the navigation with a kadence/navigation block with this id.
Zet kleuren om in de blokattributen van: Converts colors in the block attributes of all posts (or of post_ids) and in the _kad meta of the Kadence objects, using a map {"#04201a":"palette3", "#dcdcdc":"#e6e6e6"}; old is case-insensitive. Run audit-colors first to see what is there. The proposal lists every change per post and per meta key, and in skipped what is deliberately not converted, with the reason: a var(--…) that has an opacity attached (Kadence converts that to rgba, which breaks a variable), a palette name in a non-Kadence block (core does not know palette3), and a non-hex value in a Gravity Forms block. Posts get one revision per post; meta has no revisions, the old value is in changes[].from. This does not touch colors in CSS files. Two steps: first without a token, then with the token and the same input.
Zet één post in de prullenbak — nooit de: Moves one post to the trash — never permanently deletes; that stays in the admin, with a human involved. Beforehand, it searches for where the object is still in use: by id attribute (like find-usages) and, for a custom SVG, also by the icon name kb-custom-{ID}. If it is in use, no token is returned, because a reference to a post in the trash makes the block silently disappear; pass ignore_usages: true if that is intended anyway. Always `riskant` (risky), even with ignore_usages (see objections): an active element on a hook (such as the footer), the front page, the posts page, the privacy page, and a scan that failed or was capped. Useful for cleaning up objects that were created twice. Two steps: first without a token, then with the token.
Zoek de post(s) waarin een blok met deze: Find the post(s) containing a block with this uniqueID. Takes precedence over slug and search. THE way to find the counterpart on the other site after a migration: the uniqueID stays the same, the post ID does not.
Zoeken waar een Kadence-object gebruikt: Find where a Kadence object is used
Zoekt posts en geeft hun post_id terug,: Searches posts and returns their post_id, as a stepping stone to inspect-post. WARNING: "search" uses the WordPress search function, which searches title AND content — so searching for a word that appears in a block returns the post that contains that block, not just posts with that title. If you want exactly one post, use slug. Without post_type, the search covers all publicly queryable post types plus the Kadence post types. A post that is restricted by a plugin such as Members is not returned here, even if inspect-post can read it.
Zoekt posts waarvan de inhoud naar een b: Searches for posts whose content refers to a specific Kadence object. Blocks such as kadence/query, kadence/navigation, kadence/query-card and kadence/header include the object through an id attribute; this tool searches on that id. Use this before you change a shared object, to know where the change will land. The search scans post content and is therefore capped: the number of scanned posts is in the status line, so an incomplete result does not read as complete.
Zoekterm. Doorzoekt titel én inhoud. Laa: Search term. Searches title and content. Leave empty if you are searching by slug.
